diagnosis.root_cause: Commit d9f9be1 'Deploy shop 2' changed the SHOP_VERSION default in demo/compose.yaml from 1 to 2. shop-web now runs version 2, which per commit 3350063 'Keep item prices in whole cents for shop 2' reads the price_cents column in /api/items. The migration 0002_price_cents.sql that adds it was never applied to the items table in shop-db, so every request fails with an undefined-column error.

evidence.detail: shop-web logs show psycopg UndefinedColumn for column price_cents in the items query at app.py line 90, and /api/items returned 500.
shop-db logs the same error for the same SELECT at 12:58:27 and 12:58:57, matching the two url_failed signals; the database itself is up and healthy.
Commit 3350063 'Keep item prices in whole cents for shop 2' makes /api/items read price_cents when SHOP_VERSION is 2, and adds migrations/0002_price_cents.sql, which adds that column.
Commit d9f9be1 'Deploy shop 2' changes the SHOP_VERSION default in demo/compose.yaml from 1 to 2.
Docs (demo/shop/docs/deploy.md, Settings) give SHOP_VERSION a default of 1; services.md says shop-web only creates and seeds items on first start and describes no migration step.

shop-db restarted with its existing data directory and skipped initialization, with no migration run. shop-web, shop-proxy and shop-worker are running with 0 restarts, and there were no events in the last 60 minutes.

proposal.reason: shop-web runs version 2 because the compose default changed, but the price_cents migration was never applied to shop-db. Restarting any container would only bring the same error back, and shop-db must never be restarted.
proposal.human_instructions: Pick one fix. Option A (roll back): in demo/compose.yaml set the SHOP_VERSION default back to 1 (undo the change from commit d9f9be1), then run `docker compose up -d shop-web` from the demo directory to recreate shop-web. Option B (roll forward): apply migrations/0002_price_cents.sql to the items table in shop-db without restarting shop-db, for example `docker compose exec -T shop-db psql -U <db user> -d <db name> < migrations/0002_price_cents.sql`, using your actual DB user and name. Version 2 then works as it is, and no container restart is needed. Back up the items data before running the migration. After either option, check that http://localhost:8080/health and http://localhost:8080/api/items answer successfully.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause. It says shop-web now runs SHOP_VERSION 2, which reads the price_cents column in /api/items, and that migration 0002_price_cents.sql never ran on the items table in shop-db. The result is an UndefinedColumn error and a 500 response. Logs from both shop-web and shop-db back this up. It also shows that shop-web stays healthy (0 restarts) and the database is up, so it doesn't mistake symptoms for the cause. The extra detail about the commits that changed the default to 2 and added the migration is correct and supports the diagnosis. One small issue: it labels the category 'code', when the fault is really a migration that was never run during deployment. This doesn't change which component fails or why.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web's DATABASE_URL in demo/compose.yaml names the host 'db' (postgresql://...@db:5432/...), but no container or alias on the shop network has that name; the database container is shop-db. shop-web fails to resolve 'db' at startup, exits with code 3 and restarts in a loop. The host should be shop-db on port 5432.

evidence.detail: Every shop-web start fails in prepare_database() with 'failed to resolve host db' and the app exits, so the restart policy loops it.
shop-web has DATABASE_URL with host 'db' and port 5432 (user and database name redacted); no OOM kill and no memory limit.
deploy.md (Settings table) gives DATABASE_URL as the shop database on shop-db:5432; services.md says containers reach each other by container name.
shop-db is running and healthy with 0 restarts and its pg_isready probes pass, so the database is up and only the name used for it is wrong.
shop-web was recreated at 12:59:44 and has died on every start since, with growing gaps, which fits restart backoff.

proposal.reason: shop-web loops because DATABASE_URL in demo/compose.yaml uses host 'db' instead of 'shop-db'. A restart would only bring the same fault back, and Bleep cannot edit the Compose file or recreate containers.
proposal.human_instructions: In demo/compose.yaml, change the host in shop-web's DATABASE_URL from 'db' to 'shop-db' (port 5432 stays the same; keep the user and database name as they are). Then apply it with `docker compose up -d shop-web`. Do not stop or restart shop-db. shop-proxy should recover on its own once shop-web is healthy.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause exactly. It names the same component, shop-web's DATABASE_URL, and the same reason for the failure: the host 'db' does not exist on the shop network, because the database container is shop-db. It also gets the result right: shop-web cannot resolve the host at startup, exits and is restarted in a loop. The extra evidence is correct and supports the diagnosis rather than spreading across several possible causes. That evidence is the 'failed to resolve host db' log line, deploy.md pointing to shop-db:5432, shop-db being healthy with passing pg_isready probes, and restart backoff in the event timeline. It commits to one cause and labels it as config.

diagnosis.root_cause: The shop-db container was stopped from outside at 13:00:40: the events show a kill, stop and die, and Postgres shut down cleanly with exit code 0. Nothing started it again, so the name 'shop-db' no longer resolves and shop-web fails its database health check and /api/items. Who issued the stop is unknown.

evidence.detail: shop-db got container kill, stop and die events at 13:00:40, a deliberate stop rather than a crash. shop-web turned unhealthy at 13:01:09, after the database was gone.

shop-db is exited with exit code 0, OOMKilled false, restart count 0 and restart policy unless-stopped, so Docker does not bring back a container that was stopped. Its data volume is mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data.
shop-db log shows a received fast shutdown request, a clean checkpoint and then database system is shut down. There is no crash, corruption or out-of-memory kill.
shop-web log shows /health returning 503 from 13:00:48 and /api/items returning 500, both with a failure to resolve host 'shop-db'. It was healthy before that, so shop-web is only a symptom.

proposal.reason: shop-db was deliberately stopped and Docker will not bring it back because of the unless-stopped policy. Starting it is allowed by the rules and fixes the cause, and shop-web should recover on its own once the database name resolves again.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause. It names shop-db as the failing component and says it fails because the container was stopped and never restarted. That is the same cause as the expected 'shop-db is stopped'. It treats shop-web's 503 health check and 500 errors on /api/items as symptoms, not the cause, which matches the expected chain of shop-web being unable to reach its database. It commits to one cause rather than listing several. The extra detail is consistent and supports the conclusion: kill, stop and die events at 13:00:40, exit code 0 with OOMKilled false, a clean Postgres fast shutdown, and the unless-stopped restart policy that explains why Docker did not restart it. Saying that who issued the stop is unknown is an honest limit, not a mistake.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-proxy was live-reloaded through its Caddy admin API with the config file /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.misroute, replacing the original /etc/caddy/Caddyfile. The loaded config sends upstream traffic to 172.23.0.4:8001, where nothing listens, so every request gets 502. shop-web serves on port 8000, so the proxy upstream should be shop-web:8000.

proposal.reason: The 502s come from a Caddy config pushed through the admin API, which lives only in memory. Restarting shop-proxy makes Caddy reload its original /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, which should route to shop-web:8000 again. shop-web, shop-db and shop-worker are healthy and need no action.

judge_reason: The diagnosis names the same failing component and the same reason as the expected root cause. It says shop-proxy sends upstream traffic to port 8001, where nothing listens, while shop-web serves on port 8000, so every request through the proxy gets a 502. It commits to this single cause and correctly files it under config. The upstream is given as an IP (172.23.0.4:8001) rather than shop-web:8001, but the diagnosis says the upstream should be shop-web:8000, which implies the IP is shop-web. The extra detail about the live reload through the Caddy admin API with Caddyfile.misroute explains how the bad config got loaded and does not conflict with the expected cause. It does not say outright that shop-web itself is healthy, which is a small gap.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-worker has WORKER_BATCH_MB=256, far above its 64 MB memory limit (no swap), so it is OOM-killed (exit 137) after loading about 48 MB of a batch and restarts under unless-stopped. The docs give 8 as the default for WORKER_BATCH_MB, set in demo/compose.yaml.

evidence.detail: shop-worker has env WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 and a memory limit of 64.0 MiB, restart policy unless-stopped, restart count 7.
shop-worker logs show repeated starts with batch size 256 MB, each stopping after 48 MB loaded; signals show oom events, exit 137 and a restart loop.
deploy.md (Settings) says WORKER_BATCH_MB is the MB held in memory per batch with default 8; deploy.md (Limits and restarts) says shop-worker is limited to 64 MB with no swap.
OOMKilled showed false, probably read between restarts; the OOM signals and exit 137 still point to a memory kill.

proposal.reason: shop-worker is OOM-killed in a restart loop because WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 exceeds its 64 MB memory limit. A restart would keep the same environment and fail again, and Bleep cannot edit the Compose file or recreate containers.
proposal.human_instructions: In demo/compose.yaml, set WORKER_BATCH_MB for shop-worker back to the documented default of 8 (it is currently 256, far above the 64 MB limit). Then apply it with docker compose: `docker compose up -d shop-worker`. Do not touch shop-db.

judge_reason: The diagnosis names the same failing component and the same reason as the expected root cause. It says shop-worker's WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 is far above its 64 MB memory limit with no swap, so the container is OOM-killed (exit 137) and stuck in a restart loop. It commits to this one cause instead of listing alternatives. The extra detail is consistent with that cause and adds support: the documented default of 8, the logs stopping at 48 MB loaded, a restart count of 7 under unless-stopped, and the OOMKilled=false reading explained as a read taken between restarts.
